full_citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration (accessed 22 Oct 2026). International Energy Statistics, bulk file INTL.zip (annual series, 1980-2025): coal, oil, gas production and consumption in physical units; electricity generation and capacity by fuel; plus Monthly Energy Review Tables 2.6, 4.3, 6.2, 7.2a and Petroleum well-completion tables E_ERTW*.

full_citation: IAEA (2021). Spent Fuel Performance Assessment and Research: Final Report of a Coordinated Research Project (SPAR-IV). IAEA-TECDOC-1975, Vienna.
notes: READ (foreword and burnup passages). States that by the end of 2020 over 400,000 tHM of spent fuel had been discharged and that spent fuel is accumulating at about 7,000 tHM per year; German PWR discharge burnup rose from 35 GWd/tHM (1983) to 50 (1998) and 65 now. Used only as validation for modelled discharge.

full_citation: United Nations Statistics Division (accessed 25 Oct 2026). Energy Statistics Database, dataflow UNSD:DF_UNDATA_ENERGY(1.2): commodities 1100 Peat, 5110 Fuelwood, 5160 Charcoal; transactions 01 Production, GA Total energy supply, 1231 Consumption by households, 08811/08812/08821/08822 electricity and CHP transformation; annual, 1990-2024.
notes: DOWNLOADED via the SDMX REST API with the CSV Accept header (4.3 MB). Country questionnaire data; a substitute for the paywalled/restricted IEA World Energy Balances (residential final consumption of primary solid biofuels). Units: peat in thousand tonnes, fuelwood in thousand m3, charcoal in thousand tonnes (UNIT_MULT 3). Starts 1990 (peat and fuelwood for the former USSR republics from 1992). China reports no household fuelwood. Database notes: http://data.un.org/_Docs/Energy_Statistics_Database_notes_UNdata.pdf.

full_citation: International Energy Agency (2024). Coal 2024: Analysis and forecast to 2027, chapter Demand. Paris. Coal demand in the power sector 5,855 Mt of 8,687 Mt world demand in 2023 (2024 projected 8,771 Mt); China 2023 4,883 Mt, 63% power.
notes: READ (web page, 25 Oct 2026). Mass basis, so the 67.4% power share is not directly an energy share (power-sector coal has below-average calorific value); used as the 2023 anchor for coal_power_share with an assumed energy-basis value of 0.65.

short_cite: EIA International Energy Outlook, coal chapter
full_citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration. International Energy Outlook, Coal chapter (coal.pdf). Electric power accounted for 59% of world coal consumption in 2012; industrial 36%; other 4% (energy-content basis).
notes: READ (web PDF, 25 Oct 2026). Edition year taken as 2016 (the IEO whose base year is 2012 data is not stated on the extracted page; treat as approximate). Used as the 2012 anchor for coal_power_share.

full_citation: Anti-Neutrino Flux from the EdF Hartlepool Nuclear Power Plant (2023), arXiv:2301.07153. Section II.A and Table I: AGR discharge irradiation 32 GWd/t in the text and 24 GWd/t in Table I for Hartlepool 1; about 1560 MWth and 600 MWe per reactor; 3.1-3.8% 235U enrichment.
notes: READ. Preprint; the paper itself gives two discharge-burnup values (32 vs 24 GWd/t), used as the range 24-32 with central 27. Authors not extracted. Not a fuel-cycle authority; an NDA or EDF fuel specification would be better.
